title: A Terminal for the Echo
premise: Freya Lockridge, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Vesper's Rest, intercepts a distress call broadcast in a language extinct since the Collapse of 2187 — a language he somehow understands. The signal leads him to a derelict colony ship, the Echo, carrying two cryogenic populations: one faction that preserved Earth's original cultures, and one that engineered themselves into something new to survive the void. As Freya repairs the Echo's failing systems, he discovers his own memories were implanted from the ship's archives, making him neither rescuer nor stranger but the vessel of both factions' histories. In the climax, with the station's reactor failing and only power enough to wake one hold, Freya chooses to split the wake cycles and merge the two peoples' records into a single shared archive, sacrificing his own stored memories to do it. He ends the novel as a man without a past but surrounded by a found family who will help him build one.
about_author: Odile Delacroix is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent a decade listening to dead frequencies before turning to fiction. She writes about lonely people in loud universes from a coastal town where the fog does most of the talking.

chapters.title: Static Season
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A routine cargo haul through contested orbits establishes his isolation: five years alone on Vesper's Rest, talking to maintenance drones and a dead AI named Marrow. Emotional beat: loneliness worn so smooth it feels like peace.

chapters.title: The Word That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct for two centuries — and Freya translates it aloud before realizing he can't possibly know it. Emotional beat: uncanny dread blooming into hunger for answers.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Corporate scavenger drones circle the signal's source; Freya must smuggle his skiff past them, using tricks Marrow taught him. Emotional beat: first taste of risk, and the thrill of choosing danger over safety.

chapters.title: The Echo
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He boards the derelict colony ship Echo and finds two sealed cryo-holds, each labeled in a different script — one ancient, one alien-modified. Emotional beat: awe curdling into vertigo at the scale of what he's found.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between the Echo's archive recordings and Freya. He hears the last arguments of two factions before they froze: Preservers versus Adapters. Emotional beat: grief for people not yet dead.

chapters.title: Marrow's Ghost
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Back on the station, he interrogates the dying AI about the language; Marrow's fragmented logs hint the station was built to receive this exact signal. Emotional beat: betrayal — his whole life may have been staged.

chapters.title: Implant
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, fractured by memory glitches. He finds the surgical scar behind his ear and realizes his fluency is implanted — his childhood memories are archive fabrications. Emotional beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Never Born
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He searches station records for any proof he existed before five years ago and finds none. Emotional beat: hollowed-out numbness, then a stubborn decision to keep going anyway.

chapters.title: First Waking
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV (introduced), an Adapter engineer Freya revives to help repair the Echo. She wakes furious, disoriented, and immediately distrusts the human who claims to be nobody. Emotional beat: friction sparking the first fragile connection.

chapters.title: Two Grammars
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Sefa and Freya. Working together on the reactor coupling, they argue over which hold deserves waking — and discover their implanted languages overlap like family dialects. Emotional beat: grudging respect.

chapters.title: The Scavengers Come
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Corporate salvage crews board the Echo to strip its cryo-tech; Sefa and Freya stage a desperate defense using the ship's own gravity plating. Emotional beat: terror forging trust.

chapters.title: What the Preservers Kept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He wakes Tomas Ilyen, eldest of the Preserver hold, who recognizes Freya's face from the archive — as the son of the ship's designer. Emotional beat: hope that is almost too heavy to carry.

chapters.title: Father, Machine
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Archive footage reveals Dr. Elias Lockridge copied his dying son's mind-pattern into the relay technician — Freya is a reconstruction. Emotional beat: rage, then a terrible tenderness toward the father he can't remember.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Dark
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The woken colonists convene in the Echo's ruined galley to decide whose future matters; old hatreds resurface between Preservers and Adapters. Emotional beat: found family fracturing along inherited lines.

chapters.title: Reactor Hymn
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Echo's core begins terminal failure, and the countdown forces everyone to abandon ideology for labor; Sefa teaches Freya Adapter engineering songs to sync their work. Emotional beat: unity through shared hands.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Marrow reveals the final layer: Earth's transmission loop — humanity's complete cultural archive — ends in nine days unless relayed onward, and the relay needs the same power as a cryo-hold. Emotional beat: the weight of impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. The crew races to rig a three-way power split everyone's math says will fail; small sacrifices accumulate — supplies, memories, dignity. Emotional beat: exhausted solidarity.

chapters.title: The Choice of Halves
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax approach: the split fails, and Freya must choose one hold — or find a third option hidden in his own architecture, since his implanted mind is itself a storage medium. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing from despair.

chapters.title: A Terminal for the Echo
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax: Freya jacks himself into the relay as living storage, letting both holds wake at half-strength while his implanted memories burn away to carry Earth's loop outward. Emotional beat: self-erasure as an act of love.

chapters.title: White Room
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, dreamlike. He drifts through his dissolving false memories — a mother's kitchen, a red bicycle, his father's voice — saying goodbye to a life that never happened. Emotional beat: elegy for a fictional self.

chapters.title: Waking Counts
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Both holds open; four hundred strangers step into a shared dawn aboard the repaired Echo, and Sefa pulls a blank-eyed Freya from the jack, refusing to let him be a casualty. Emotional beat: fierce, chosen belonging.

chapters.title: New Grammar
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV closing chapter. Months later, the Echo's community broadcasts Earth's loop onward and begins writing its own archive — with Freya, memoryless but loved, recording the first entry in a language they're inventing together. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope.
